definition: A group of values in a grouped frequency table, written as an inequality such as $20 \le t < 25$; the classes leave no gaps and don't overlap, so each value belongs to exactly one class.
A chart of grouped data on a continuous scale, with one bar per class and no gaps between bars; when every class has the same width, each bar's height is the class frequency.
The number of data values less than or equal to a given value, a running total of the frequencies; on a cumulative frequency graph it is plotted at each class's upper boundary.
The middle value of the data when it is put in order; with an even number of values it is the mean of the middle two.
The $k$th percentile is the value with $k\%$ of the data below it, so the median is the 50th percentile.
The largest data value minus the smallest, a single number that measures spread; it is not the range of a function.
A diagram drawn to scale with a box from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$, a line at the median, whiskers out to the smallest and largest values that are not outliers, and a cross for each outlier.
